sections.h2: Where is the Hertford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Go to the third floor of the Hertford County Courthouse, 119 Justice Drive, Suite 9, in Winton. The office phone is 252-358-7850, and hours run from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM Monday through Friday except county holidays and closings.

The county says its staff maintain real estate documents going back as far as 1862, and its history page notes land deeds in the area dating to 1710. The office holds deeds, deeds of trust, maps, military discharge records, notary records, and birth, death and marriage records for events in Hertford County.

The county sits in northeastern North Carolina, bordering Virginia to the north. Farming remains its economic backbone, with tobacco, cotton, peanuts, corn and soybeans listed as staples, and the Chowan River crosses its land. QuickFacts lists 353.16 square miles of land.

sections.h2: How did Hertford County's land records begin?
sections.html:
The General Assembly formed the county in 1759 from land taken from Bertie, Northampton and Chowan counties. Before that the area was part of the Parish of Saint Barnabas. The first court met at Cotton's Ferry, and Winton, on the Chowan River, replaced it as seat of government when the town was incorporated in 1766. Ahoskie grew later into the commercial center of the county.

Two highways cross in the county, U.S. 13 running north and south and U.S. 158 running east and west. The county's records are indexed by name, which is how a lawyer follows an old farm tract back through its owners.

sections.h2: What does Hertford County post as its recording fees?
sections.html:
The posted schedule carries a warning that fees can change. Make checks payable to the Hertford County Register of Deeds and put a working phone number on them; mailed returns need your own stamped envelope addressed to yourself.

Real estate lines from the Hertford County Register of Deeds fee schedule
ItemPosted charge
Deeds and general instruments$26.00, first 15 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00, first 35 pages; $4.00 per extra page
Excise tax on deeds$2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price
Satisfactions and cancellationsNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 per document
Several instruments in one packet$10.00 extra

Plat copies are $3.00 a page. Copy requests made by fax or online cost $1.00 for page one, then $.25 for each page after.

sections.h2: Which formatting rules can trigger the Hertford County nonstandard fee?
sections.html:
The recording rules page repeats the paper standards of G.S. 161-14. A document that misses them is still recorded, with the $25.00 fee added.

  • Letter or legal size paper, one side only
  • Black type on white, 10 point or larger
  • Wide blank band across the head of page one

Session Law 2011-351 adds a drafter rule: page one of a deed or deed of trust must name the person or law firm that prepared it. The county also wants the tax parcel pin on each deed, plus either a tax department stamp showing no delinquent taxes or a sentence directing the closing attorney to pay any back taxes from closing proceeds. Electronic deeds must carry the sentence.

sections.h2: Can a Hertford County deed be e-recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. Everything except maps can be e-recorded, according to the county FAQ, and the e-recording page names Corporation Service Company and Simplifile as submitters. The recorded copy comes back electronically right after recording.

Your closing attorney picks the route.

sections.h2: What can the Hertford County office not do for a seller?
sections.html:
The list matters more than people expect, because sellers often call the register for help it cannot give.

  • It cannot search a title, because state law bars register staff from doing so. An individual or a legal representative can run the search.
  • It cannot confirm whether a lien exists. A deed of trust recorded in the office is the sign that the property secured a loan.
  • It cannot change a recorded deed. A new deed must be prepared, and the office recommends seeing an attorney.
  • It cannot name an owner from a street address, since records are indexed by name. Land Records Mapping, at 252-358-7809, handles location questions.
  • It holds no estate, will or divorce records. Those sit with the Clerk of Superior Court, 252-358-7100.

Real estate documents are online, though older indexes and images may not be.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax in a Hertford County sale?
sections.html:
The seller. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the burden on the transferor, and the county prints $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price on its schedule.

Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance reaches later purchasers and lien creditors only once it is registered, so recording should follow signing quickly. The statutes are at G.S. 105-228.30 and G.S. 47-18.

sections.h2: What else is handled at the Winton counter?
sections.html:
The same office issues licenses and certificates, and the fee schedule and FAQ list the details. Knowing them helps if a seller also needs paperwork for an estate or a move.

  • Marriage license: $60.00, issued from 8:30 AM until 4:30 PM, valid for sixty days. A couple can buy it in Hertford County and marry anywhere in North Carolina.
  • Magistrate wedding: $50.00, arranged through the magistrate at the sheriff's department.
  • Certified birth, death or marriage copy: $10.00 each, with a government photo ID. Only close relatives or an authorized agent can pick one up.
  • Online vital record requests: $3.50 added, through the county's Get Certificate Now program.
  • Notary oath: $10.00. The Secretary of State sends the notice and no appointment is needed.
  • Beer licenses: $5.00 off premises and $25.00 on premises. Wine licenses: $25.00.
  • Military discharge filing and certified copy: free, though discharges are not open to public viewing.

sections.h2: How small is the Hertford County housing market?
sections.html:
The head count dropped from 24,669 in 2010 to 21,552 in 2020 and is estimated at 19,015 for mid 2025. Housing stock stands at 9,873 units, and the county issued just 3 building permits in 2025.

  • Median home value among owners, 2020 to 2024: $119,200
  • Share of owner households: 67.4 percent
  • Rent at the midpoint: $844
  • Household income at the midpoint: $45,537
  • Seniors 65 or older: 27.1 percent

Values are modest, so fixed charges such as recording fees weigh more on a small sale. Ask your closing attorney for the full list of closing costs before you set a price. Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How does the 2027 revaluation touch deeds recorded now?
sections.html:
The county's revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, the first since 2019, and field measuring began in July 2025. Deeds recorded before and after that date use the same recording steps. What changes is the assessed value attached to the parcel.

The Tax Assessor and Tax Collector sit at 115 Justice Drive in Winton. Ask the collector about the current bill before you close. The county also warns the public about deed scams, with a fraud detection page linked from the Register of Deeds site.

faqs.q: How much does Hertford County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $26.00 for a general instrument up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per page after that, and $64.00 for a deed of trust up to 35 pages. Call 252-358-7850 to check for changes.

faqs.q: What is the excise tax on a Hertford County deed?
faqs.a: The county lists $2.00 per $1000.00 of purchase price, and the seller pays it.

faqs.q: What happens if my Hertford County deed is formatted wrong?
faqs.a: It is recorded anyway, with a $25.00 non-standard fee added. Review the rules above first.

faqs.q: Can Hertford County staff search my title or find a lien?
faqs.a: No. State law keeps register staff from searching titles, and the office will not say whether a lien exists. An attorney or title professional can read the recorded instruments.

faqs.q: Can I get a copy of my recorded deed in Hertford County?
faqs.a: Yes, at the counter or on the county sites, though older indexes and images may be missing online. Certified copies are priced per page.
